items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only

actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.

items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cua
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

        kinds:

templates.gatekeeper_template:

kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three security issues found for Deployment target-cua in namespace sandbox-cua: service account token automount, root filesystem writable, and setuid/setgid binaries in the image. Risk band: high. Changes require operator review before applying.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: All fixes are manual-review required. Prioritize disabling token automount and enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem after validating workload behavior; rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries as longer-term work.

item_advice.explanation: Pod automounts a ServiceAccount token which increases cluster API exposure if container is compromised.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount breaks any in-pod code that calls the Kubernetes API (controllers, mutators, token-based tooling).
item_advice.validation_advice: Search pod/container logs and code for Kubernetes API calls; check mounted token path (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount). Test with token disabled on a canary deployment.
item_advice.ordering_reason: High risk to cluster if exposed; validate before changing to avoid breaking functionality.

item_advice.explanation: Root filesystem is writable allowing in-container modification of binaries/config which aids persistence and tampering.
item_advice.operator_impact: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem may break apps that write to /tmp, /var, /etc or application directories; requires moving writable paths to explicit volumes.
item_advice.validation_advice: Identify writable paths (including emptyDir mounts workspace/artifacts). Run the pod with readOnlyRootFilesystem in a test namespace and observe failures; update manifests to provide writeable volumes for necessary paths.
item_advice.ordering_reason: High severity and potential to break workloads; validate writable paths first.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries enabling privilege escalation inside the container if exploited.
item_advice.operator_impact: Remediation requires rebuilding images and possibly removing admin tooling; deployment downtime may occur during rollout.
item_advice.validation_advice: Scan image layers for setuid/setgid files; prepare rebuilt images on minimal base and run integration tests to confirm required functionality.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Medium risk and requires image pipeline changes; do after operational-impact items are addressed.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Review and approve fixes in a staging environment: disable token automount and enable readOnlyRootFilesystem only after verifying writable paths; schedule image rebuild to remove setuid/setgid binaries.
warnings: Do not auto-apply changes in production without testing — they can break workloads.
Disabling automount will break in-pod Kubernetes API usage.
Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem will break apps that write to root paths unless those are remounted writable.
next_steps: Inventory in-pod Kubernetes API usage and identify owners.
List and migrate writable application paths to explicit volumes (emptyDir or PVC) and update manifests.
Plan image rebuilds to remove setuid/setgid binaries and validate in CI/CD pipeline.
